subject: dragonflyBrooch
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: dragonfly.
Style: art nouveau Lalique jewellery.
reasoning:
I'm planning a dragonfly design in Art Nouveau Lalique jewellery style, thinking through realistic proportions—roughly 7cm body length and 9cm wingspan matching real-world scale unless the brief calls for stylized sizing.

For materials I'm imagining translucent plique-à-jour enamel wings with gold wire veins, gemstone eyes (opal, amethyst, peridot), and a gold segmented body. For the pose, I'm settling on a perched stance with wings spread flat and all six legs touching the ground at y=0, with the thorax sitting at a small height above that, keeping the overall proportions modest but functional for the joint and segment detailing.

Now I'm laying out the skeleton: a thorax root joint feeding into an abdomen chain of ten segments acting as the tail, plus a head with separate upper labrum and lower jaw/mandible joints for the mouth. For the four wings I'm planning three-joint chains per wing with membrane geometry extruded from an outline, aiming for that glassy translucent plique-à-jour look.

Since materials here are opaque with alpha-cutoff, I'm thinking of achieving the plique-à-jour effect using a texture with real transparent cutouts—drawing the wing as a gold-wire network with open cells, some left clear and others filled with teal, green, or amber enamel, very Lalique in style. I'll render this on double-sided cards leaned flat and rigged to the wing joint frames so the wings bend naturally with the skeleton.

Working out how the wing card geometry attaches to the bone frame, with the root at the bottom, tip at top, and the correct mirroring for the opposite wing side.

Actually, since gold wire veins and transparent windows need alpha, I should use two textured planes back-to-back instead of extruding geometry, which also solves the double-sided visibility issue and lets me control orientation through the up-vector mapping to the drawing's top edge.

I realize the mirrored wing orientation needs fixing so the leading edge faces correctly on both sides, so I'll generate a mirrored version of the wing texture using a transform, then work out the back plane's axis orientation for the opposite wing.

I work out the texture assignment rule: tex = (s*face>0) ? A : B, verifying each of the four combinations of wing side and front/back face gives the correct leading-edge orientation. Then I note the two coplanar back-to-back planes need a tiny physical separation so each front face only renders from its own side.

For the wings themselves, each becomes a simple two-joint rigid chain (root and tip) with the plane geometry attached to the root. I want to add real 3D detail beyond the texture: a gold costa rod running along the leading edge from root to tip, plus a small dark enamel pterostigma box near the tip, giving the wings tangible bling on top of the vein texture.

For the eyes, I'm going with cabochon glass spheres using a radial-gradient SVG texture in peridot green-teal tones to suggest faceted compound eyes, with a subtle emissive glow (around 0.35) rather than anything too intense, keeping with the Lalique opal/glass aesthetic.

For proportions, I'm sizing the wings larger than realistic for a dramatic stylized look (length ~0.07, chord ~0.02), with the body running from the head near the front to a long slender abdomen tapering to a total length of roughly 0.13.

Now I'm scaling the body like a hawker dragonfly (7-8cm), setting head, thorax, and abdomen positions, and working out leg placement and IK chain lengths so the three leg pairs reach naturally from the thorax to the ground with proper femur-tibia-tarsus proportions.

Checking the reach distance confirms the legs are workable, so I'm setting up the bend direction for the limb IK—using a single outward-and-upward bend vector applied to the joint, wrapped as a one-item list to match the expected array format, then figuring out the correct sign convention for left versus right side.

I'll rely on world-space coordinates rather than local() to avoid left/right confusion, reserving local offsets only for things like head placement. For the chain construction, I need to match joint names to the points returned by the limb function—since three segment lengths produce four points (root, two joints, end), I'm working out how the three names should correspond to the spans between them.

Still thinking through chain naming...

Let me plan a part budget around 180–340 pieces total, starting with the thorax as a loft or ellipsoid base shape, plus small spike spines along the tibia and a tiny sphere for each foot tip.

For the thorax itself, I'm going with a low-poly scaled sphere painted gold with enamel diagonal stripes to echo the dragonfly's banding, plus a gold collar ring at the neck and a jeweled cabochon on top in the Lalique style — gold, enamel, opals, horn, glass palette.

Now I'm defining the abdomen as a 10-segment tapered chain curving slightly from the thorax back, with eight joints driving the sweep geometry along the body.

Placing gold rings at segment boundaries using evenly spaced frames along the sweep, plus small gold stud jewels positioned at segment centers using the surface normal points, orienting the torus geometry along the tangent direction at each location.

For the ring size I need to account for the torus's flat-faced octagon shape versus the circular sweep boundary, so bumping the radius to about 1.06R plus tube thickness should cover any gap since slight hiding won't be noticeable in the final jewelry piece.

Now I'm planning the gold tail claspers and abdomen tip, then moving to the head: positioning the thorax and head centers, and sizing the two large eye spheres so they meet at the midline with a wrapped texture.

For the eye texture, I'm figuring out the sphere's UV seam orientation so the drawing's middle faces outward on each eye — using rotation [0,-90,0] for one eye and [0,180,0] for the mirrored eye so the facet pattern points the right way.

Now I'm designing the eye texture itself as a stained-glass mosaic dome: a radial gradient from peridot to dark teal, gold hex-lattice facet lines, and a bright cabochon highlight offset toward the upper area, drawn in a 200x100 viewBox with the visible front half mapped to the central portion of the texture.

Then I'm placing small face pieces — an amber frons/labrum under the eyes and a labrum box below that — positioning them with precise offsets.

Now I'm working out the skeleton hierarchy: head attaches to thorax, jaw attaches to head, and I'm adding ocelli as three tiny opal spheres on the forehead plus delicate gold-wire antennae with pearl, drop-shaped tips in a Lalique style. I'm deciding the thorax itself should be the root joint (named "thorax" with a spine-like role) with the abdomen chain and wing joints branching off it, working out their exact coordinate offsets.

Defining wing joint positions...

Working out the plane normal by projecting up perpendicular to the wing axis, then deriving the local orientation vectors so the geometry's drawing axes align consistently with the earlier coordinate convention.

I confirm the rule holds for the back face too by checking the sign of the cross product's z-component, which tells me whether to use texture A or B based on where the leading edge falls. Now I'm sizing the wing outline drawing itself, using a width-to-length ratio of about 0.35 for the viewBox.

Writing SVG path...

I'm mixing opaque stained-glass cells with open plique-à-jour windows, then working out how to generate the vein grid programmatically using interpolated leading/trailing edge functions and banded subdivisions along the wing.

I'm planning roughly 100 polygon cells per wing with straight cloisonné-style edges, needing four mirrored textures for forewing/hindwing pairs with distinct teal/violet color themes, plus an eye and gem texture bringing the total to 7-8 svg assets. I'm also adding a small dark enamel stigma polygon near the leading edge tip of each wing.

Working out the leading and trailing edge curve functions...

Still tuning wing curve formulas...

The outline is traced from leading edge sweeping to the tip and back along the trailing edge, drawn as a gold-stroked polygon, with tip rows degenerating into triangular cells as chord width hits zero. For fills, I'm working out probability rules per cell based on position u and k, aiming for a Lalique dragonfly feel—deep teal near the base transitioning into translucent greens and blues toward the tip with randomized fill thresholds.

Each filled cell picks a color from a palette biased by position along the wing, blending base amber/peridot tones near the root into teal further out. I'm adding a smaller inner polygon shrunk toward the centroid and lightened to mimic enameled cabochon facets, plus working out where the pterostigma mark sits near the wingtip.

I'm also sizing the SVG rasters for the texture atlas and sketching a leading-edge costa rod in 3D, figuring out the perpendicular in-plane direction to position it correctly relative to each wing's orientation.

Working out the leading edge rod placement, running from the wing joint position offset toward the lateral edge, over to the center point with a small radius for the rod geometry.

I'm adding small gold hinge spheres and gem cabochons at each wing base, four total, then considering whether to add further detail to reduce wing flatness before moving on to the thorax design — a gold-based enamel sphere shape.

Writing thorax paint logic...

Working through the leg attachment points, I'm checking they sit correctly against the thorax ellipsoid surface, adjusting the hip y-coordinate until the math places them just inside. Then I'm sizing the feet so the tapered leg tubes end near the ground plane.

Now I'm sizing the head details — eyes as spheres positioned on either side of the head joint, with a smaller frons/clypeus shape at the front of the face, working out exact coordinates so the eye surfaces and face piece meet up correctly.

I'm placing the labrum as a tiny box under the frons, then setting up the mandible as a jaw joint with small wedge-shaped jaw parts and tiny gold tooth spikes, followed by adding three ocelli jewels near the top of the eyes.

I'm working out the geometry where the eye spheres meet at the top center to find the natural valley for the ocelli cluster, then placing a gold-green forehead dome sphere with three small opal ocelli spheres nestled just above it.

Now I'm adding the antennae: curved paths with gold wire segments rising from the forehead up and forward, capped with tiny pearl beads at the tips, swept along bone-weighted paths attached to the head.

For the abdomen, I'm shaping it as an art-nouveau whiplash curve -- an S-curve that lifts and curls slightly upward at the tail end, giving the perched dragonfly a graceful rising silhouette rather than a flat pose.

I'm now setting up the abdomen's segment chain, parenting it to the thorax with eight named segments, then defining a radius profile that swells at the base, narrows into a slim waist, and clubs slightly before tapering to a fine point at the tip.

Writing abdomen ring colors...

Adding amber accent spots, then tallying up the part counts for abdomen (rings, studs, cerci, tip pearl) and thorax (sphere, gem, collar torus, wing base cups and gems) to estimate total geometry pieces.

Then for the head I'm counting eyes, frons, labrum, jaw segments, ocelli, antennae with beads, and gold bezel torus rings around each eye — roughly 20 pieces. Legs come out to about 42 pieces across six legs with spines, feet, and knee gems, and wings add roughly 24 more between wing planes, costa rods, extra veins, and bases.

Running total is around 140, so I want to push toward 180-340 by adding Art Nouveau filigree -- gold whiplash scrolls on the abdomen and thorax shoulders, extra longitudinal vein rods per wing for relief, pearl beads at leg knees, and a gold wire sweep along each wing's trailing edge, aiming for roughly 200 total pieces.

Working out the 3D math for mapping wing points: converting the flat texture coordinates into root-plus-span-plus-chord vectors so veins and the trailing edge wire follow the correct curvature, then sweeping rods along specific chordwise fractions to place the vein lines in 3D space.

Rods at k=0, 0.32, 0.68, 1, with cross-veins jittered on rows only. I'm positioning rods centered on the plane thickness with radius 0.0005 so they bridge both front and back faces evenly, then sweeping a catmull curve through the rod points to generate each vein geometry.

I'm orienting each wing plane using the root-to-tip vector, keeping a slight dihedral lift at the tip for a gentle upward curve, and making sure the wing's local axes stay perpendicular so the texture maps correctly to the rod positions.

I'm giving forewings a teal-peridot-aqua-amber palette while hindwings lean sapphire-amethyst-teal-amber, keeping both cohesive but distinct. For the eye texture I'm building a faceted sphere with an SVG hex-lattice pattern over a radial gradient fading from yellow-green center to deep teal edges, with gold-stroked hexagon facets overlaid.

I'm thinking dragonfly eyes often shift tone vertically, so I'll use a gradient from blue at top through teal to peridot green at the bottom. I'll skip adding a bezel ring and instead consider using a gilt metal paint from the clockwork kit for the gold patina look on the body.

For the legs, I'll apply gilt and brass metal paints, keeping the noise texture size small (around 0.02m) since the parts are tiny and I want to avoid the gradient looking flat across such a small surface. I'm checking texel density math to make sure the painted area stays under the 4000 texel/m cap, landing around 0.25mm resolution, and confirming the flat color palette stays within the 64-color limit before adding small octahedron studs along the abdomen.

Now I'm working out how to place these studs using the sweep's frame data, calling stick with the geometry, color, and hit point, and considering alternating peridot and amber coloring via the `along` helper that iterates frames without using the callback's return value. I'm also adding lateral gem spheres at 90 and 270 degree offsets along a few segments to cover both sides symmetrically, then starting to build an abdomen ring using torus geometry anchored to a chain point.

Thinking through torus placement for the segment rings — rigging each ring to its nearest chain joint via the bone property so skinning stays rigid, computing radius as a scaled version of the local body radius, and setting a thin tube thickness with low-poly flat shading for a faceted look. Now I'm positioning a thorax collar torus near the neck junction, reasoning about z-depth so it sits correctly between the head and thorax without poking through either.

For legs, I'm working out the limb function calls that take a hip root, foot target, segment lengths, and a knee-bend direction hint, then checking distances between hip and target against total leg length to confirm the knee will bend convincingly. I'm laying out front, mid, and hind leg targets with different x/z offsets so the dragonfly's legs splay forward and backward naturally, and tuning the knee hint vector to push the bend outward and upward.

Writing femur sweep radii...

Adding a tiny jewel sphere at the knee joint for each leg.

For the bone fallback I'll use leg.tip with a non-null assertion. I also need small claws at the foot—tiny spikes pointing forward-downward—though I should be careful they don't poke below the floor plane.

Working out the claw placement so the spike tips stay just above y=0, with two claws per foot angled slightly differently, giving twelve spikes total.

For the limb chains I'm confirming the joint-to-tip counts match up correctly (hip, knee, ankle, foot), then setting up the wing joints as a two-point polyline chain.

Now I'm placing the wing plane geometry on its bone, positioning it with a slight offset along the normal and orienting its axes using the plane's direction vectors.

For the wing plane dimensions, I'm keeping a consistent 1:3 width-to-length ratio across forewing and hindwing, using viewBox proportions to compute actual sizes like L=0.066, W=0.022 for the forewing and similarly scaled values for the hindwing.

I'm planning a function that generates each wing's SVG texture based on wing type, mirroring, palette, and seed, memoizing four textures total so the left/right pairs stay visually consistent.

Building the vein grid rows now, using vertex-based jitter so adjacent quads share deformed points instead of a rigid uniform mesh, giving the veins a more irregular, natural look.

Writing cell fill logic...

Writing pterostigma polygons and mirroring logic...

Gems should glow since they have flat colours, and wings could get a subtle plique-à-jour glow to mimic light passing through enamel, giving a lit-glass effect without flattening the shading too much. Eyes being textured parts should glow fine in their own colors, while the painted thorax can't take glow. Now I'm starting the thorax paint function, defining depth and side variables based on position.

Adding more palette colors like peridot, amber, amethyst, and sapphire, then thinking about how to color the head parts—using mottled teal-green tones for the forehead and defining the labrum jaw piece.

Checking mandible positioning against the labrum and joint offsets, then verifying the head joint placement and frons coverage relative to the eye and thorax alignment.

Now I'm considering Art Nouveau filigree touches, thinking about adding small gold spiral scrolls on each side of the thorax as decorative whiplash curls, similar to Lalique-style jewelry details.

The sign of the turn doesn't matter much for symmetry here, so I'll just keep turns at -s*1.3 for both sides. Now I'm checking that the scroll sits properly against the thorax surface at x=±0.0118, verifying the ellipsoid extent at the relevant z-offset stays consistent with the scroll's radius so it hugs the body correctly.

Placement-wise, the legs and hips go underneath, the scrolls sit at mid-side, and wings root at the top — that arrangement works. For the cerci at the tail, I'm positioning two small gold spikes at the abdomen's end point, using the tail path's final tangent direction (adjusted slightly outward) to orient them, with the spike's base aligned to the rounded end cap of the tail sweep.

I'm placing a tiny pearl at the tip of each cercus and possibly a small bead between them for extra detail, though I should keep these additions minimal given the overall tiny scale of the model, trusting the viewer to auto-fit regardless. I'm using a rod helper function to connect two points with a given radius, color, and bone binding for the skeletal rig.

Now I'm setting up the module exports with the meta object defining name and description, then starting to write the actual import statements and build logic in TypeScript, pulling in the needed helper functions from the builder library while trimming out anything I won't actually use to avoid unused-import errors—settling on importing things like createBuilder, rng, limb, paint, mix, svg, catmull, spiral, and metal.

Building the joint hierarchy...

Defining abdomen radius keyframes...

Writing abdomen paint logic...

Adding abdomen ring tori...

Now I'm adding dorsal studs along the abdomen sweep, alternating amber and peridot octahedrons at each of ten evenly spaced points, embedded slightly and possibly glowing.

I'm also placing lateral bead spots at a few segment positions on either side of the sweep, then starting to build the thorax sphere with bone attachment, offset position, and non-uniform scale for shaping.

Now I'm adding an amethyst gem on the dorsal thorax, offset and scaled for a tilted glow, with a gold torus bezel wrapping around its base.

The collar torus would float oddly around the neck gap, so I'm dropping it in favor of a small gold bead sphere at the neck joint instead. For the wings, I'm placing a tiny gold cup sphere at each root with a small teal gem accent, positioned symmetrically along the thorax.

Now I'm defining the wing geometry, working out root and tip positions for the fore and hind wings on each side, calculating the thorax surface curvature at the root points to position them correctly against the body.

Working out the wing axis and width geometry...

Confirming the right-handed axis convention holds, so I should generate fresh geometry per part rather than reusing one, and I'm working out how the draw-right direction for texture A should line up with the lateral axis so the leading edge matches physically.

For the mirrored texture B, I'm figuring out that the vein position still needs to map to the same physical lateral location despite the flipped drawing orientation. I'm planning a shared `wingShape(kind)` helper at module scope to give consistent wing dimensions and point functions for both the SVG and 3D builds, then setting up the rod points for veins across the wing using a small set of u/k sample positions.

Working out rod thickness, sweep paths, and texture definitions...

Now I'm defining the wing textures as fore/hind pairs with normal and damaged variants, each generated via SVG using a seeded RNG for randomized vein patterns...

Writing wing shape SVG code...

I'm checking the chord formula for continuity at the junction points, verifying the curve matches smoothly where the two branches meet for both forewing and hindwing.

Writing texture grid generator...

Still building color helpers and SVG assembly...

Still writing the stigma polygon and starting the eye texture gradient definition...

Still writing SVG code...

I'm placing the two eye spheres symmetrically on the head with mirrored rotation, checking that their textured gradient faces outward correctly and that the slight overlap between them doesn't cause visual artifacts.

Now I'm picking colors for the head segments—teal enamel for the frons, gold for the forehead dome, amber for the labrum—and setting up the antennae as curved bone-attached paths with tapering radius and bead tips.

Writing leg loop code...

I'll use a single bend direction for the joints, specify the foot contact point on the floor plane, and sweep the leg with a tapering radius profile using a gilded metal finish.

Adding spike and knee jewel details...

Now I'm adding claws to each foot, choosing a forward or backward direction based on whether the leg is a front or hind one, then placing small spikes rooted at the foot center.

Checking the leg geometry to make sure the tube radius and foot sphere don't dip below the floor plane, confirming the lowest points stay just above zero. Now I'm setting up the filigree scroll positions, iterating over left/right sides and front/back z-positions to compute their centers.

For each wing I'm adding small gold base cups at the root joint with a glowing gem colored teal or amethyst depending on whether it's a fore or hind wing. Then for the tail I'm planning cercus spikes and a pearl near the end of the abdomen, plus maybe tiny gold crests on the first abdominal segments.

Now I'm weighing a few more decorative touches -- gold leaf-shaped Art Nouveau accents on the abdomen top, maybe cheek pearls or eye bezels on the head -- but keeping part count reasonable (~170), so I'll settle for adding a row of ten tiny gold beads along the underside of the abdomen to complement the existing lateral beads.

I'm double-checking the API usage: confirming `flat: true` works for `b.stick`, that `rotation` passes correctly into `b.part`, that `glow` wraps a part and returns it properly, and that `b.along` callbacks can return void since I'm just placing sticks inside. I'm also verifying the TypeScript shape of the sweep point object to make sure `t`, `n`, and `tangent` are accessible as expected.

Now I'm working out the thorax paint function, trying to create dorsal gold stripes using position and normal data to define banding patterns, then simplifying toward a cleaner rule based on horizontal distance from center to pick between lighter and darker gold tones.

Checking the gilt metal color against the flat gold string to confirm they're close enough, then verifying wing paths accept point arrays as polylines, sweep options for sides and caps, and bone attachment syntax for head and abdomen joints all look correct against the API.

Confirming the `up` parameter signature is right, and double-checking that my cross product computation properly clones vectors to avoid mutation. I'm now writing the helper function that computes rod positions along the wing shape by interpolating between the root point scaled along the wing axis and lateral vectors based on wing width and height ratios.

I'm verifying the wing's aspect ratio and tip positioning match the texture coordinates, then checking that the rod point list along the u-parameter and the radii mapping by index are consistent with the 3D vein positions on the vertex grid.

Noting the hindwing tip offset, then double-checking the paint function's return type union and confirming all SDK imports (createBuilder, rng, limb, paint, mix, svg, catmull, spiral) and the grid typing are correct before writing the final code.
